panels.visual: The busy Agora market of Athens, 399 BC: Socrates (old, bald, snub nose, bulging eyes, pot belly, barefoot, shabby cloak) cheerfully questioning a proud general in a plumed helmet, a crowd gathering
panels.caption: In 399 BC an old man called Socrates spent his days in this Agora, asking questions.

panels.visual: The general tangled up in his own words, sweating, a thought bubble full of knots; the crowd laughing
panels.caption: He showed that even important men did not really know what they were talking about.

panels.visual: Young men following Socrates eagerly with scrolls, while their angry fathers and two rich politicians glare from a doorway
panels.caption: Young people loved it. Their parents and powerful men did not.

panels.visual: Three accusers pointing at Socrates in front of a court building, one shaking a scroll
panels.caption: He was put on trial: for not respecting the gods, and for corrupting the young.

speech.speaker: Accuser
speech.text: He is a danger to Athens!

panels.visual: A huge jury of ordinary Athenian men dropping bronze voting discs into two urns, the 'guilty' urn fuller
panels.caption: 501 citizens voted. Most said guilty. The sentence was death.

panels.visual: Socrates standing calm and unafraid in front of the jury, one finger raised, light on his face
panels.caption: He would not beg for his life.

speech.speaker: Socrates
speech.text: A life without questions is not worth living.

panels.visual: A dim prison cell at night: his rich friend Crito whispering urgently through the bars, a bribed guard looking away, a boat waiting in a thought bubble
panels.caption: In prison, his friend Crito had a plan to get him out.

panels.visual: Socrates sitting on his prison bed shaking his head gently, Crito in tears
panels.caption: Socrates refused.

speech.speaker: Socrates
speech.text: I have lived by the laws of Athens. I will not run from them now.

panels.visual: The jailer, sad-faced, handing Socrates a cup of hemlock; his friends around the cell crying into their cloaks; Socrates calm
panels.caption: On the last day he drank the hemlock calmly. His friends wept.

panels.visual: Socrates lying on the bed under his cloak, the jailer pressing his feet; a cold blue tint creeping up from his feet towards his knees
panels.caption: He walked about, then lay down. The cold crept up from his feet.

panels.visual: Socrates uncovering his face for a moment to speak to Crito; a small inset of a rooster
panels.caption: His last words were about a debt.

speech.speaker: Socrates
speech.text: Crito, we owe a rooster to Asclepius. Pay it.

panels.visual: Today: archaeologists' excavated stone foundations in the Agora, a case of tiny clay medicine bottles in the foreground, Glauka the owl pointing with a wing
panels.caption: Plato wrote it all down. In the Agora, archaeologists found a building with tiny medicine bottles: maybe his prison.
